# openmetadata_document (Resource)

Manages an OpenMetadata document (knowledge panel). Documents are standalone articles whose contents live in a free-form JSON payload.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openmetadata_document" "getting_started" {
  name                 = "getting-started"
  entity_type          = "KnowledgePanel"
  fully_qualified_name = "getting-started.acceptance"
  display_name         = "Getting started"
  description          = "Onboarding notes for the data platform."
  data = jsonencode({
    title = "Getting started"
    body  = "Read this first."
  })
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `data` (String) Document payload as a JSON object. Whitespace and key order are normalized once the document is read.
- `entity_type` (String) Document flavour, for example KnowledgePanel. Changing it replaces the document.
- `fully_qualified_name` (String) Fully qualified name, sent to the server verbatim. Changing it replaces the document.
- `name` (String) Document name. Changing it replaces the document, because the name is fixed at creation.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Markdown description of the document.
- `display_name` (String) Human-readable name shown in the OpenMetadata UI.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time in RFC 3339 format.
- `updated_by` (String) User that performed the last update.
- `version` (Number) Server-side entity version.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by UUID.
terraform import openmetadata_document.getting_started 1f6a3a52-8d34-4f4b-9d0f-2f1c1c1c1c1c

# Or import by fully qualified name.
terraform import openmetadata_document.getting_started getting-started.acceptance
```
